newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says may import more Malaysian olein.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says may import more Malaysian olein.

text.p: Indonesia has taken delivery of 38,000 tonnes of the 52,000 tonnes of palm olein it planned to import from Malaysia until January, the official Antara news agency reported on Friday.
The agency quoted Beddu Amang, head of the state logistics agency BULOG, as saying the government would import more olein from Malaysia if local prices could not be controlled.
He said the domestic price of palm olein, a crude palm oil based cooking oil, was currently 1,450 rupiah/kg, compared with 1,400 rupiah a year ago.

Antara said the government had also requested the state-run Joint Marketing Agency, which markets all the crude palm oil produced by state plantations, to supply BULOG with 30,000 tonnes of crude palm oil.

Amang said BULOG would have stocks of about 48,000 tonnes by January, when Moslems in Indonesia observe the Ramadan fasting month that preceeds Eid al-Fitr. Moslems constitute about 80 percent of the country's nearly 200 million people.
